answer: Epochal Equihash admission puzzles deter Sybil swarms in agent networks trading saffron yields, meadow moisture, and coastal tide data. Each epoch, a node finds a generalized-birthday collision bound to its public key and a randomness beacon, which peers verify in microseconds with a few hashes. Every fake account thus incurs verifiable DRAM capacity and memory-bandwidth costs per renewal. Yet adversaries with rented GPU clusters or botnets can still mint many parallel identities.
